articles.title: New Raiders Rumors Reveal Team's Stance on Kirk Cousins Trade Amid Vikings Speculation
articles.summary: ESPN's Adam Schefter isn't buying into speculation that the Minnesota Vikings could look to reunite with Kirk Cousins ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
articles.body:
ESPN's Adam Schefter isn't buying into speculation that the Minnesota Vikings could look to reunite with Kirk Cousins ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

"[Cousins] is the perfect mentor to their No. 1 pick who they don't want to rush along, and who they want to leave on the bench... Why are the Raiders trading Kirk Cousins to Minnesota? Why are they doing that?" Schefter asked around the 22:00 mark of Thursday's episode of the Adam Schefter Podcast.

Schefter concluded, "It makes no sense to me."

The Raiders have since gotten off to a 4-4 start behind Cousins, who has completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 2,124 passing yards, with 2026 top pick Fernando Mendoza serving as his backup.

He ranks second in the NFL with 19 touchdown passes with just five interceptions through Week 8.

The Athletic's Michael Silver asked earlier this week if the Vikings could explore a trade for Cousins or the Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones in the wake of Kyler Murray's hamstring injury.

"My sense is that nothing has been ruled out," Silver reported.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero said Wednesday on KFAN he felt there was a "low percentage change" the Vikings took a big swing at the trade deadline.

Should the Raiders choose to stick with Cousins to continue pushing for the top of the AFC West while Mendoza continues focusing on his development, the Vikings would have to either seek another quarterback in the next five days or rely on Carson Wentz until Murray is able to return.

Wentz is currently on track to start when the Raiders kick off their Week 9 matchup at the San Francisco 49ers Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026-27, Standings, Bracket Scenarios After Jaguars vs. Ravens
articles.summary: With Week 9 of the NFL season underway, we've officially reached the halfway point in the 2026 campaign, and the playoff picture is starting to come together.
articles.body:
With Week 9 of the NFL season underway, we've officially reached the halfway point in the 2026 campaign, and the playoff picture is starting to come together.

On Thursday, the Jacksonville Jaguars continued their stronghold of the struggling AFC South, improving to 6-2 with a win over the Baltimore Ravens.

The Ravens, meanwhile, dropped to 4-5, and their playoff hopes are dwindling as they continue to be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson.

Ahead of the rest of Week 9 on Sunday and Monday, here's a look at how things are shaking out.

Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, Lead AFC South)

Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, Lead AFC North)

Josh Allen and the Bills are in control of both the AFC and the AFC East amid a dominant start to the 2026 campaign, but they can't relax just yet as they try to secure a wild-card bye.

The second half of Buffalo's schedule is relatively daunting, with matchups against the Vikings, Chiefs, Patriots, Bears and more on the way.

The Steelers and Broncos are only a game ahead in their respective divisions, so they can't afford to take their foot off the gas.

The Jaguars are sitting comfortably ahead of the Pack in the AFC South, with the 2-5 Texans sitting in second place. Jacksonville should have no trouble winning its second consecutive division crown.

The race for the division crown is most definitely still on for these four squads.

The Chiefs looked like the team to beat through the first few weeks, but back-to-back losses suggest they're not quite the Super Bowl contenders they appeared to be. Still, any team led by Patrick Mahomes has a shot, and they're just a game back from the Broncos.

The Patriots beat the Bills earlier this season and could very well dethrone them for the AFC East title, and the matchup between those two on Dec. 6 will have plenty of implications.

The Bengals, meanwhile, have looked like playoff contenders; it's just a matter of staying consistent.

The bottom half of the AFC is pretty weak this year, and aside from the Brown, Raiders and Ravens, most of these teams have virtually no chance of reaching the playoffs.

San Francisco 49ers (6-1, Lead NFC West)

The Niners and Vikings are the only two teams in the NFC that have truly looked dominant through the early going. Minnesota's success perhaps comes as a surprise, as it appeared to be in for a rebuilding year, but nonetheless, Kevin O'Connell has his group looking like a contender.

The Giants being atop the NFC East says less about how good they are and more about how bad the rest of the division is. They're the only team above .500 and still have not beaten a team with a winning record.

The same can be said of the Panthers, but they're not far ahead of the Buccaneers and Falcons.

The entirety of the NFC North appears capable of making a Super Bowl run, which makes it arguably the most interesting divisional race to watch. If all four teams reach the playoffs, it would mark NFL history.

The defending champion Seahawks and the new-look Rams both came into the season expecting to compete for a Super Bowl, but injuries have them both off to a rough start. If they can get their rosters healthy, both NFC West squads could turn things around.

The Bucs and Falcons still have a path to the postseason thanks to their weak division, while the Cowboys and Commanders could also both say the same.

articles.title: Ravens were down to their third QB and had a predictably ugly performance in blowout loss to Jaguars
articles.summary: The Ravens had to prepare for Thursday night with their top two QBs on injured reserve.
articles.body: It was sad watching the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday night. The Ravens were a Super Bowl contender not long ago. Many thought they could bounce back from a bad year and be a top team again this season. It's a reason they were scheduled for a prime-time game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. But Lamar Jackson got hurt early this season, then got hurt again last Sunday, and Tyler Huntley got hurt too. That left the Ravens to play undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, their third quarterback, on Thursday night. He played through an injured ankle and ended up having to deal with a rainstorm most of the night. He was the Ravens' only option left, and the results were predictable. The Jaguars caught the Ravens at the right time and had an easy night in a 33-10 win. The Ravens finished with 57 yards passing. The Ravens (4-5) have decisions to make before the trade deadline. They are reportedly on the verge of dealing for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and while that will make them a functional offense, it's unlikely Brissett saves the season. Jackson might return from a right thumb injury but that's no guarantee, and the Ravens might be well out of the race by the time he is healed anyway. Thursday night was an uncompetitive, bad game. The Jaguars (6-2) are clearly one of the best teams in the NFL this season, but practically any team would have defeated Baltimore on Thursday night. There wasn't anything the Ravens or Fagnano could do, no matter how many tricks they had in the game plan. It was an unwinnable situation, which might be the case for the rest of their season too. Ravens try to get trickyThe Ravens opened in a wildcat formation with Derrick Henry getting the first snap of the game at quarterback. There were more wildcat plays, extra linemen and any other tricks the Ravens could figure out. Henry even had a pass completion on the first drive. No amount of trickery was saving the Ravens. The Jaguars are a good team with a strong defense and Baltimore couldn't move the ball. The rain didn't help. Baltimore had 27 yards passing in the first half. Its longest completion was 7 yards and its longest play was 9 yards in the first two quarters.Baltimore was trying to stay in it until Jacksonville hit a big play late in the half. Against a blitz, Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington downfield, and he was in the clear to run for a 50-yard touchdown. Lawrence had 197 passing yards in the first half, more than six times what his counterpart Fagnano had at halftime. Washington's touchdown made the score 17-3. It's hard to count an NFL team out with a half to go, but it was hard to believe Baltimore would score 14 more points, much less outscore Jacksonville by 14. Jaguars pull awayComing out of halftime, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter optimistically told Amazon Prime Video he wanted to see his offense score on the first drive and see what happened after that. The Ravens threw an interception on the first drive. The Ravens were trailing 20-3 when they got a break, as Travis Hunter fumbled and Baltimore recovered near midfield. But the Ravens couldn't get a first down, and on fourth-and-inches tight end Mark Andrews, lined up for what looked like a tush push, fumbled the snap. It looked like he was going to turn and hand it off but it didn't matter because he couldn't hold onto the ball. It was that kind of night. The Jaguars caused some of those issues too. Their defense is very good, and the offense is capable of putting up a lot of points if there's not a downpour of rain. They have a good chance of making a deep playoff run. The same could have been said about the Ravens before Jackson's latest injury. Brissett will be an upgrade over what we saw against the Jaguars, but there was a reason he was demoted to third string by Arizona this week and then was available in a trade. The Ravens' season probably isn't going anywhere. Things could look even worse in Baltimore by Tuesday's trade deadline.

articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars cruised to a 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday night.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars cruised to a 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday night.

Baltimore was unable to emerge victorious with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center, as starter Lamar Jackson and backup passer Tyler Huntley were both sidelined with injuries .

The Jaguars ended up winning after entering the game as 9.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Jacksonville didn't waste much time jumping out in front on Thursday, opening the game with a 77-yard drive that was capped off by a short touchdown run from Bhayshul Tuten.

The Ravens cut into the early deficit with a 53-yard field goal on their first drive, but the Jaguars quickly pushed their lead back to seven points with a 36-yard field goal of their own.

Baltimore's offense failed to respond for the remainder of the first half, as all three of its possessions in the second quarter ended with punts.

Meanwhile, Jacksonville gained a 17-3 advantage before halftime after Trevor Lawrence connected with Parker Washington for a 50-yard touchdown.

Rainy conditions impacted both offenses during the second half, as the only score of the third quarter was a 45-yard field goal by Jaguars kicker Cam Little.

Little connected on two more field goals to start the fourth quarter before Jacksonville put the finishing touches on the lopsided victory with Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s two-yard rushing touchdown.

Ravens running back Justice Hill immediately responded with a 65-yard score, but a late comeback never materialized.

Baltimore's offense struggled mightily throughout the contest, finishing with just 10 first downs and 227 total yards. The Ravens also committed three turnovers and converted a mere four of 14 opportunities on third down.

Jacksonville maintained its lead atop the AFC South standings by improving to 6-2, while Baltimore dropped to 4-5.

articles.summary: The NFL's Week 9 slate is its last before the 2026 trade deadline on Nov. 10. Organizations across the league will be evaluating their own roster, as well as the 31 other lineups.
articles.body:
The NFL's Week 9 slate is its last before the 2026 trade deadline on Nov. 10. Organizations across the league will be evaluating their own roster, as well as the 31 other lineups.

Case in point, the Baltimore Ravens already made a move by trading for quarterback Jacoby Brissett prior to Thursday's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley injured and Brissett not up to speed, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano led the Ravens offense. The game went as expected. Baltimore won't be the only franchise dealing with quarterback upheaval this weekend.

Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow all of the weekend's action to break down the biggest stories and ask the most pressing questions coming out of each contest.

Jacksonville Jaguars at Baltimore Ravens

The Jacksonville Jaguars, the Juggernaut

The Jacksonville Jaguars aren't mentioned among the league's elite squads. They need to be. Liam Coen's team may have come up short during their 2025 postseason appearance, but this roster has been outstanding since November of last year.

Thursday's 23-point victory over the Baltimore Ravens became the Jaguars' fourth double digit win this season—which leads the NFL and doubles the league's next-best squad. Furthermore, Jacksonville also has a league-leading eight wins by 20 or more points since the start of the 2025 campaign, according to NFL Researcher .

While the Jags were on the road during their latest outing, Jacksonville has been particularly dominant when playing at EverBank Stadium with seven straight wins by 17 or more points.

Depending on Monday's outcome for the Buffalo Bills, the Jaguars could be tied atop the AFC standings with an opportunity to claim homefield advantage throughout the 2026 postseason.

Will the Jaguars Be Active at the Trade Deadline?

With Thursday's performance, the Jaguars now own a 6-2 record and sit comfortably atop the AFC South. Jacksonville has the potential to be quite active before Tuesday's trade deadline, as a buyer and seller.

To the Jags credit, the league's best run defense slowed Derrick Henry and allowed him to run for only 57 yards. Yes, Justice Hill broke off a 65-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, but the game was already out of hand. Even so, Jacksonville is in the market for defensive tackle help after DaVon Hamilton suffered a torn quadriceps, according to ESPN's Ian Rapaport .

Furthermore, wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. may be as good as gone. The former 1,000-yard receiver wasn't targeted once during Thursday's contest. He's officially caught one pass during his last four appearances.

Is Joe Fagnano Experience Already Over for Baltimore Ravens?

Joe Fagnano's first start served as a wonderful underdog story of an undrafted rookie who didn't expect to make the Ravens' roster coming out of training camp. He did and was thrust into Baltimore's starting in Week 9 as Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley recover from injuries.

A great story doesn't automatically equate to a fairytale ending. In Fagnano's case, he's likely a one-and-done starter after throwing for 60 yards and two interceptions during Thursday Night Football .

Granted, the wet evening made life more difficult on the first-year quarterback. But it was clear the Ravens weren't going to put the ball in his hands anyway. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle built the offensive gameplan through Derrick Henry.

Meanwhile, Jacoby Brissett now has 11 days between games to prepare as QB1 after being acquired in a trade from the Arizona Cardinals.

Ravens Experience Another Significant Injury

As if missing a roster's top two quarterbacks isn't enough, the Ravens best defensive player, Kyle Hamilton, left Thursday's contest with a hip injury and didn't return to the game.

Hamilton is a two-time first-team All-Pro. His ability to move around like a chess piece serves as the rudder for the Ravens defense. His 10 tackles for loss/stops at the line of scrimmage are the most among safeties this season, according to Pro Football Focus .

If Hamilton is forced to miss any time, Baltimore's defense will look drastically different.

Sunday's action will be the final indicator of who will be buyers and who will be sellers prior to Tuesday's trade deadline. Though a few have already been determined prior this weekend's matchups. Everyone is looking at you, Indianapolis Colts.

Monday Night Football: Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings

How does an NFL team bench its starting quarterback without calling it a benching? Ask the Minnesota Vikings. Carson Wentz will start Monday against the Buffalo Bills. Officially, Wentz will now be QB1 because Kyler Murray is dealing with hamstring tightness. Wentz took over the offense in Week 1 when Murray suffered a concussion. His inclusion may help since Minnesota continues to struggle offensively. However, a matchup against the Bills means Josh Allen will be on the same field, making life much more difficult on an opponent, even if it features an elite defense.

articles.title: 'No Excuses,' Ravens HC Reacts to Blowout Loss to Jaguars After Lamar Jackson Injury
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wasn't interested in using the absence of star quarterback Lamar Jackson as an excuse for the team's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wasn't interested in using the absence of star quarterback Lamar Jackson as an excuse for the team's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday.

"Obviously it's a tough situation for our guys," Minter told reporters after the game. "But, I just told them there's no excuses. There's no whatever, we don't have this guy, we don't have that guy. We've got to make a decision again over this break, got a little bit of a break for the guys to mentally reset and come back and seek improvement in all three phases. That's what we'll be after."

With Jackson out due to a right thumb injury and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley sidelined with a toe injury, the Ravens turned to undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano under center.

Fagnano finished 10-of-18 for 60 yards and two interceptions against Jacksonville.

"I'm not here to make excuses," Fagnano said after the game, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. "We just didn't execute. I have to play better."

He was appearing in the second game of his career, as he previously threw for 91 yards while getting picked off once during the Ravens' 36-10 defeat at the hands of the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.

Baltimore's offense was only able to muster three points through three quarters against Jacksonville, finally finding the end zone with a 65-yard rushing touchdown by Justice Hill as the Jaguars held a 33-3 lead in the fourth.

The Ravens picked up just 10 first downs while committing three turnovers during the contest. They averaged 4.2 yards per play.

Baltimore has now lost four consecutive games since opening the season with a 4-1 record.

The Ravens' struggles without Jackson have been particularly disappointing considering the two-time MVP started the year by completing 70.1 percent of his passes for 967 yards and six touchdowns compared to one interception. He also rushed for 144 yards and one score.

Baltimore will now look to bounce back in its next game, a matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16.

articles.title: ‘Feels Like a No-Brainer,’ ‘Packers Should Call Baltimore’ — NFL World Weighs In on Derrick Henry Trade Rumors After Ravens’ TNF Loss
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are clearly struggling to keep their season on track, and their latest loss has raised questions about whether Derrick Henry still fits...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are clearly struggling to keep their season on track, and their latest loss has raised questions about whether Derrick Henry still fits their plans.

With the trade deadline approaching, the discussion has moved beyond one bad night in Baltimore. NFL insiders and analysts are now weighing whether Henry could finish the season somewhere else.

NFL Insiders React to Derrick Henry Trade Rumors After Ravens' Loss

Baltimore's 33-10 defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night gave trade speculation fresh momentum.

The Ravens fell to 4-5, with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both on injured reserve. Rookie Joe Fagnano managed just 60 passing yards and threw two interceptions in his first NFL start, leaving Henry without much support from the passing game.

Henry, who ranks 15th in PFN NFL RB Impact , finished with 57 rushing yards on 17 carries. He has failed to reach 60 yards in four consecutive games and is now averaging 3.9 yards per carry, a career low. With his 33rd birthday approaching in January, his timeline may not match Baltimore's uncertain season.

Clay Travis believes the Ravens should consider moving him rather than wasting the remaining years of his career. He posted on X , "The Ravens should trade Derrick Henry to a contender. The season is done, and Henry doesn't have that many years left to play. Feels like a no-brainer."

Pittsburgh Steelers writer Jarrett Bailey also identified a possible destination, suggesting , "The Packers should call Baltimore about Derrick Henry."

The speculation gained more weight when A to Z Sports' Austin Stanley reported interest from two teams. He wrote , "Derrick Henry could be playing his last game with the Baltimore Ravens tonight. Sources tell A to Z Sports that two teams have emerged with serious interest in trading for the future Hall of Fame running back before next week's trade deadline. Keep both eyes open on this one."

Another reporter, John Frascella, posted , "Yeah… Derrick Henry bout to be on a different team."

NFL reporter Justin Ramos also saw a potential deal as a tad more realistic after the loss, writing , "I think right after this game that the Ravens could actually trade Derrick Henry."

Patriots-focused radio host Nick Cattles questioned the financial and roster value of such a move for New England, despite praising Henry's ability. "Derrick Henry is one of the best. But this makes no sense: RB is WAY down the priority list. You have only so many assets to deal after AJB. He turns 33 in January and has a $16.2M cap hit next year. Thanks, but no thanks," Cattles wrote .

Henry's contract could make him an attractive deadline acquisition. His 2026 base salary is just $1.3 million, leaving approximately $650,000 for a new team to pay over the remainder of the season. He is also scheduled to receive $12 million in non-guaranteed compensation in 2027, including an $11 million base salary and a $1 million roster bonus.

The New England Patriots, New York Giants, and Minnesota Vikings have been linked to potential backfield upgrades in reports.

With the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching, Baltimore must decide whether Henry remains part of its plans or could bring back useful draft capital.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk’s 49ers Comeback Takes Unexpected New Turn
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk finally appeared ready to end his standoff with the San Francisco 49ers this week — but him returning might not be that easy. The former All-Pr...
articles.body:
finally appeared ready to end his standoff with the San Francisco 49ers this week — but him returning might not be that easy.

The former All-Pro wide receiver filed for reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list on Wednesday and plans to report to the 49ers' facility on Friday afternoon, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

"Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field," Rosenhaus said.

It was widely expected to set the stage for his release, which would allow Aiyuk to sign elsewhere. However, there's a $13 million problem standing in the way.

Brandon Aiyuk Could Owe 49ers $13 Million

Aiyuk's push to get released could be complicated by roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture he owes the 49ers, according to NFL Network's Tom Pelissero.

"Veteran WR Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture — a potential complication in his efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday," Pelissero posted on X .

"The NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association are both involved in attempting to resolve the situation. The sides could reach an agreement to pay back the money, or it could go to arbitration. But it's complicated and may take time to resolve."

Aiyuk could simply pay back the money in order to move on and sign with another team. If he elects to try his luck with arbitration, things could drag out for a while.

In other words, showing up on Friday probably won't settle anything.

The 49ers presumably have been eyeing that money for months. NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco estimated back in July that the team could claw back anywhere from $13.8 million to $18.4 million of the $23 million signing bonus Aiyuk received in 2024, which is prorated at $4.6 million per year.

"Not only will the 49ers not have to pay him another penny, whereas if he had just shown up, the 49ers would have been on the hook for $27 million for this year, it also enables the 49ers to get a lot of money back," Maiocco said on the "49ers Talk" podcast.

San Francisco has paid Aiyuk $48.1 million since he signed his four-year, $120 million extension in August 2024. He's played seven games since.

Aiyuk hasn't played since tearing his ACL, MCL, and meniscus against the Kansas City Chiefs in October 2024.

Things reached a boiling point during his rehab. The 49ers voided about $27 million in guarantees last summer after Aiyuk failed to meet attendance and rehab requirements.

They then placed him on the reserve/left squad list in December. Since he was on that list when his $24.9 million option bonus for 2026 came due, the 49ers didn't have to pay it.

Aiyuk didn't help his cause this past offseason either. He called out the team in a series of social media posts. He wrote on Instagram in July that he would not be "reinstating with them nor ever doing any kind of business with them."

Head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch have both said Aiyuk won't play for the 49ers again.

So a release still appears to be the likeliest outcome. Lynch has also said he'd trade Aiyuk to any team that wants him. But previous attempts went nowhere, and the trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10.

"I have no expectation," Shanahan said Wednesday when asked about Aiyuk's return, adding he didn't expect a resolution before Friday.

Still, the 49ers have made it clear they're in no rush. They've been content to let Aiyuk sit on the list with zero pay for 11 months, and Pelissero's report suggests they won't let him walk away without getting something back.

So how badly does Aiyuk want to play again?

articles.title: ‘For what?’ – NFL fans can’t believe latest Lamar Jackson contract update
articles.summary: The latest reports about Lamar Jackson’s Ravens future have fans on social media more than a little riled up. Lamar Jackson has been placed on injured reserv...
articles.body:
The latest reports about Lamar Jackson's Ravens future have fans on social media more than a little riled up.

Lamar Jackson has been placed on injured reserve following the injury to his thumb. This has severely impacted the Baltimore Ravens, who are also dealing with an injury to backup QB Tyler Huntley. Another year of big expectations will likely end up in disappointment.

Jackson is no longer a young QB. He is 29 years of age and is supposed to be well in the middle of his prime. However, health issues have become a big narrative over the past couple of seasons. With that in mind, his next contract has become a contentious topic among fans.

Lamar Jackson in line to become NFL's 'highest-paid' star ever and Ravens fans are questioning it

In 2023, Jackson signed a 5-year, $260 million deal with the team. That runs out in 2027, meaning that the team has a big decision to make. Despite his struggles, it would be unexpected if the Ravens chose to move on from Lamar. However, the alternative might be pretty bad too.

According to a recent report from NBC Sports, the team could be on the hook to pay Jackson some big money once again and this time, a lot of fans don't like the idea.

"For what? To sit on the bench for more than half the season?" one fan asked. "And how will you pay for good offensive line to protect him or good wide receivers/tight ends?" another questioned. "This would be the dumbest move I've seen in a while, he's made of glass," a third fan commented.

"The Ravens won't win a Super Bowl with Lamar, so stop wasting everyone's time," a different comment read. "Only way this is working is if they win a ring in 2028 and that's probably not happening," claimed a fifth fan. "I love Lamar but this is a terrible idea," a sixth fan simply said.

Jackson's future is unlikely to lie away from Baltimore, but he has a lot of leverage when it comes to contract negotiations. Despite his recent injury record, QBs like Lamar aren't easy to replace. The Ravens have a massive decision on their hands.

articles.title: Packers’ Evan Williams credits red-hot Green Bay defense for winning Defensive Player of the Month
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers enjoyed a stellar October month which saw them win four of their five matches to bring themselves up to 5-3 for the season. And well, a...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers enjoyed a stellar October month which saw them win four of their five matches to bring themselves up to 5-3 for the season. And well, as a result of what has been an impressive season thus far, safety Evan Williams was named NFC Defensive Player of the Month for October after recording 41 tackles, two interceptions, four passes defended, one sack, three quarterback hits and a fumble recovery.

Williams himself credited the red-hot Packers defence for the award , per a post on X by Matt Schneidman.

"Pretty good, pretty good, it's definitely a blessing man, even be considered for something like that," he said. "I feel like it's really more of a group award than anything. We say when we're all succeeding, that's when individuals start to see success … it's a blessing to receive some recognition like that."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Williams was selected in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL draft , and is currently having a breakthrough year. Williams became the third safety since 2000 to record at least 40 tackles and three takeaways in a single month, and the first to accomplish the feat since 2011.

Williams posted a 90.9 overall defensive grade in October, the highest among NFL defenders, while recording 31 solo tackles, six pressures, 10 defensive stops and three turnovers. He allowed just seven completions for 58 yards on targets in coverage, surrendered no touchdowns and gave up a passer rating of 21.1.

Williams received his first Defensive Player of the Month award and became the third Packers safety to win the NFC honor, joining Xavier McKinney in 2024 and Atari Bigby in 2007. Green Bay has now had a player win the October award in three consecutive years, with Micah Parsons receiving it in 2025 and McKinney in 2024.

The Packers will now travel to Gillette Stadium to take on the New England Patriots, and will hope to continue their stellar run in November.

articles.title: Tom Brady explains why Brock Purdy deserves MVP consideration as 49ers impress
articles.summary: Tom Brady has named Brock Purdy among his MVP candidates after the San Francisco 49ers quarterback impressed during the first half of the NFL season. Purdy h...
articles.body:
Tom Brady has named Brock Purdy among his MVP candidates after the San Francisco 49ers quarterback impressed during the first half of the NFL season.

Purdy has helped guide the 49ers to a 6-1 record through seven games, despite the team dealing with several injuries on the offensive side of the ball.

The 26-year-old has completed 69.2% of his passes for 1,748 yards, 15 touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also added 161 rushing yards and one touchdown on 32 carries.

Tom Brady backs Brock Purdy's MVP case after impressive San Francisco 49ers start

Brady shared his MVP candidates in his weekly power rankings for Fox Sports, although the NFL legend admitted he was reluctant to make an early prediction.

The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback named four players who have caught his attention: Purdy, Josh Allen, Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs.

"There's nothing I like less than trying to figure out who's the MVP not even halfway through the season," Brady said.

However, he was particularly impressed by what Purdy has done in San Francisco, highlighting how important the quarterback has been to their winning record.

"Brock Purdy, the 6-1 Niners, I don't think they would be in that position without Brock's steady dependable consistent play. He's done so many great things," Brady added.

Purdy was selected with the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft, earning the label of 'Mr. Irrelevant'. His performances since entering the league have made that tag look increasingly misplaced.

49ers general manager John Lynch has also praised the quarterback's development, particularly his ability to extend plays and make improvements to his game.

"He's extremely talented," Lynch said. "You see him, the way he goes and extends plays. He's done it in each and every game, aside from being able to stay in the pocket and progress."

Lynch also suggested Purdy had taken criticism about his throwing ability personally, pointing to the improvements he has made in driving the ball downfield.

With Brady now including him in the MVP conversation, Purdy has another endorsement to add to his growing reputation. Maintaining his current production will be important as San Francisco looks to protect its strong start.
